findings.title: Double interpolation risk when runSplitQuery is called from shardQuerySplitting
findings.body: runSplitQuery now applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables to each query. However, shardQuerySplitting.ts also calls applyTemplateVariables on queries before invoking runSplitQuery (via runSplitQuery -> runSplitGroupedQueries). This means queries get interpolated twice: once in runShardSplitQuery and again inside runSplitQuery. If applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent (e.g. for variables with special characters, regex escaping, or variables that get consumed/removed on first pass), this could produce corrupted queries or double-escaping, and is wasteful. This also changes order relative to shard selector interpolation (interpolateShardingSelector happens before the second applyTemplateVariables call), which may re-process the shard selector unexpectedly.

findings.title: Loss of per-query metadata/order from applyTemplateVariables map
findings.body: The new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` is applied to all non-hidden, non-empty queries uniformly, but applyTemplateVariables for sharded/interpolated selector queries previously happened in a different place with different context. No test covers interaction with scopedVars per-query differences (e.g., when `request.filters` is combined with sharding-specific values), so there's a test gap for the combined sharding + ad hoc filter + split scenario.

findings.title: Interpolated queries passed into runSplitQuery for re-interpolation
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates queries via applyTemplateVariables and passes them to splitQueriesByStreamShard, which eventually calls runSplitQuery with already-interpolated expressions (including shard selector interpolation via interpolateShardingSelector). Since runSplitQuery itself now calls applyTemplateVariables again on its targets, the shard-selector-modified expr (containing __stream_shard__ labels) will be run through applyTemplateVariables a second time. If applyTemplateVariables performs operations that aren't safe to re-apply (e.g., stripping/escaping of variable syntax, or relies on original unmodified expr), this could silently break shard-filtered queries or produce incorrect results that aren't caught by existing tests focused only on happy-path interpolation of $__auto/$step variables.
